+ # GTU-C312 CPU and OS Simulator
+ 
+ This project implements a simple CPU simulator with a custom instruction set (GTU-C312) and a basic operating system that supports cooperative multitasking.
+ 
+ ## Project Structure
+ 
+ - `cpu/` - CPU simulator implementation
+   - `cpu.cpp` - Main CPU implementation
+   - `cpu.h` - CPU class definition
+   - `instruction_set.h` - Instruction set definitions
+ - `memory/` - Memory system implementation
+   - `memory.cpp` - Memory management
+   - `memory.h` - Memory class definition
+ - `os/` - Operating system implementation
+   - `thread_manager.cpp` - Thread management
+   - `thread_manager.h` - Thread management definitions
+   - `system_calls.cpp` - System call implementations
+ - `main.cpp` - Main program entry point
+ 
+ ## Building and Running
+ 
+ ```bash
+ mkdir build
+ cd build
+ cmake ..
+ make
+ ./cpu_simulator
+ ```
+ 
+ ## Features
+ 
+ - Custom CPU instruction set (GTU-C312)
+ - Memory-mapped registers
+ - Thread management with cooperative multitasking
+ - System calls implementation
+ - Debug mode with memory tracing
+ - Context switching between threads 
```

+ #ifndef INSTRUCTION_SET_H
+ #define INSTRUCTION_SET_H
+ 
+ #include <cstdint>
+ 
+ // Instruction opcodes
+ enum class Opcode : uint8_t {
+     // Arithmetic instructions
+     ADD,    // Add two registers
+     SUB,    // Subtract two registers
+     MUL,    // Multiply two registers
+     DIV,    // Divide two registers
+     
+     // Memory instructions
+     LOAD,   // Load from memory to register
+     STORE,  // Store from register to memory
+     
+     // Control flow
+     JMP,    // Unconditional jump
+     JZ,     // Jump if zero
+     JNZ,    // Jump if not zero
+     
+     // System calls
+     SYSCALL,// System call
+     
+     // Other
+     HALT    // Stop execution
+ };
+ 
+ // Register indices
+ enum class Register : uint8_t {
+     R0 = 0,
+     R1 = 1,
+     R2 = 2,
+     R3 = 3,
+     R4 = 4,
+     R5 = 5,
+     R6 = 6,
+     R7 = 7,
+     PC,     // Program Counter
+     SP,     // Stack Pointer
+     FLAGS   // Status Flags
+ };
+ 
+ // System call numbers
+ enum class SyscallNumber : uint8_t {
+     YIELD = 0,  // Yield CPU to another thread
+     EXIT = 1,   // Exit current thread
+     PRINT = 2   // Print value from register
+ };
+ 
+ // CPU flags
+ struct Flags {
+     bool zero : 1;
+     bool carry : 1;
+     bool overflow : 1;
+     bool negative : 1;
+ };
+ 
+ #endif // INSTRUCTION_SET_H 
```

_**User**_

i will keep sending you the pdf npw The CPU
Your CPU (named GTU-C312) has a very small and non-typical instruction set.
IntructionExplanation
SET B ADirect Set : Set the Ath memory location with number B. Example: SET -
20, 100 writes the value of -20 to memory location 100.
CPY A1 A2Direct Copy: Copy the content of memory location A1 to memory A2.
Example: CPY 100, 120 copies the memory value of address 100 to the
memory address 120
CPYI A1 A2Indirect Copy: Copy the memory address indexed by A1 to memory
address A2. Example: CPYI 100, 102: if memory address 100 contains
200, then this instruction copies the contents of memory address 200 to
memory location 120.
ADDAdd number B to memory location A
A B
ADDI A1 A2Indirect Add: Add the contents of memory address A2 to address A1.
SUBI A1 A2Indirect Subtraction: Subtract the contents of memory address A2 from
address A1, put the result in A2
JIF A CSet the CPU program counter with C if memory location A content is lessthan or equal to 0
PUSH APush memory A onto the stack. Stack grows downwards.
POP APop value from stack into memory A.
CALL CCall subroutine at instruction C, push return address.
RETReturn from subroutine by popping return address.
HLTHalts the CPU
USERSwitch to user mode
SYSCALL PRN ACalls the operting system service. This system call prints the contents of
memory address A to the console followed by a new line character. This
system call will block the calling thread for 100 instruction executions.
SYSCALL HLTCalls the operting system service. Shuts down the thread
SYSCALL YIELDCalls the operting system service. Yields the CPU so OS can schedule
other threads.
The numbers in the above instruction sets are signed long intergers, which means that ADD 300 -1
can be used as an instruction to decrement the memory location 300 value by 1.
The parameters for the instructions can be memory locations (A, A1, A2), unsigned long numbers
(B), or instruction numbers (C).

+ #include "memory.h"
+ #include <iostream>
+ 
+ Memory::Memory(uint32_t size) : memory(size, 0) {}
+ 
+ int64_t Memory::read(uint32_t address) const {
+     if (!isValidAddress(address)) {
+         throw MemoryError("Invalid memory address: " + std::to_string(address));
+     }
+     return memory[address];
+ }
+ 
+ void Memory::write(uint32_t address, int64_t value) {
+     if (!isValidAddress(address)) {
+         throw MemoryError("Invalid memory address: " + std::to_string(address));
+     }
+     memory[address] = value;
+ }
+ 
+ void Memory::clear() {
+     std::fill(memory.begin(), memory.end(), 0);
+ }
+ 
+ void Memory::dump(uint32_t start, uint32_t end) const {
+     if (!isValidAddress(start) || !isValidAddress(end) || start > end) {
+         throw MemoryError("Invalid memory range for dump");
+     }
+     
+     for (uint32_t i = start; i <= end; i++) {
+         std::cout << "Address " << i << ": " << memory[i] << "\n";
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ bool Memory::isValidAddress(uint32_t address) const {
+     return address < memory.size();
+ }

Now, let's implement the CPU class to execute these instructions:


---

```diff
- 
+ #include "cpu.h"
+ #include <iostream>
+ 
+ CPU::CPU(std::shared_ptr<Memory> memory) 
+     : memory(memory), debug_mode(false), instruction_count(0) {
+     reset();
+ }
+ 
+ void CPU::reset() {
+     state.program_counter = 0;
+     state.stack_pointer = memory->getSize() - 1;  // Stack grows downwards
+     state.mode = CPUMode::KERNEL;
+     state.halted = false;
+     instruction_count = 0;
+ }
+ 
+ void CPU::step() {
+     if (state.halted) return;
+     
+     int64_t instruction = fetchInstruction();
+     executeInstruction();
+     
+     if (!state.halted) {
+         state.program_counter += 3;  // Each instruction takes 3 words
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ void CPU::run() {
+     while (!state.halted) {
+         step();
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ void CPU::halt() {
+     state.halted = true;
+ }
+ 
+ void CPU::printState() const {
+     std::cout << "CPU State:\n";
+     std::cout << "Program Counter: " << state.program_counter << "\n";
+     std::cout << "Stack Pointer: " << state.stack_pointer << "\n";
+     std::cout << "Mode: " << (state.mode == CPUMode::KERNEL ? "KERNEL" : "USER") << "\n";
+     std::cout << "Halted: " << (state.halted ? "Yes" : "No") << "\n";
+ }
+ 
+ void CPU::printMemory(uint32_t start, uint32_t end) const {
+     memory->dump(start, end);
+ }
+ 
+ int64_t CPU::fetchInstruction() const {
+     return memory->read(state.program_counter);
+ }
+ 
+ void CPU::executeInstruction() {
+     int64_t instruction = fetchInstruction();
+     Opcode opcode = static_cast<Opcode>(instruction);
+     
+     if (debug_mode) {
+         std::cout << "Executing instruction: " << static_cast<int>(opcode) << "\n";
+     }
+     
+     switch (opcode) {
+         case Opcode::SET: {
+             int64_t value = memory->read(state.program_counter + 1);
+             int64_t address = memory->read(state.program_counter + 2);
+             memory->write(address, value);
+             break;
+         }
+         case Opcode::CPY: {
+             int64_t src = memory->read(state.program_counter + 1);
+             int64_t dst = memory->read(state.program_counter + 2);
+             memory->write(dst, memory->read(src));
+             break;
+         }
+         case Opcode::ADD: {
+             int64_t address = memory->read(state.program_counter + 1);
+             int64_t value = memory->read(state.program_counter + 2);
+             memory->write(address, memory->read(address) + value);
+             break;
+         }
+         case Opcode::PUSH: {
+             int64_t address = memory->read(state.program_counter + 1);
+             memory->write(state.stack_pointer, memory->read(address));
+             state.stack_pointer--;
+             break;
+         }
+         case Opcode::POP: {
+             int64_t address = memory->read(state.program_counter + 1);
+             state.stack_pointer++;
+             memory->write(address, memory->read(state.stack_pointer));
+             break;
+         }
+         case Opcode::HLT:
+             halt();
+             break;
+         default:
+             std::cerr << "Unimplemented instruction: " << static_cast<int>(opcode) << "\n";
+             halt();
+             break;
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ void CPU::handleSyscall(SyscallNumber syscall_num) {
+     switch (syscall_num) {
+         case SyscallNumber::PRN: {
+             int64_t address = memory->read(state.program_counter + 1);
+             std::cout << memory->read(address) << "\n";
+             instruction_count = 0;  // Reset instruction count for blocking
+             break;
+         }
+         case SyscallNumber::HLT:
+             halt();
+             break;
+         case SyscallNumber::YIELD:
+             // Will be implemented with thread management
+             break;
+         default:
+             std::cerr << "Unknown syscall: " << static_cast<int>(syscall_num) << "\n";
+             break;
+     }
+ } 
```

The CPU
Your CPU (named GTU-C312) has a very small and non-typical instruction set.
IntructionExplanation
SET B ADirect Set : Set the Ath memory location with number B. Example: SET -
20, 100 writes the value of -20 to memory location 100.
CPY A1 A2Direct Copy: Copy the content of memory location A1 to memory A2.
Example: CPY 100, 120 copies the memory value of address 100 to the
memory address 120
CPYI A1 A2Indirect Copy: Copy the memory address indexed by A1 to memory
address A2. Example: CPYI 100, 102: if memory address 100 contains
200, then this instruction copies the contents of memory address 200 to
memory location 120.
ADDAdd number B to memory location A
A B
ADDI A1 A2Indirect Add: Add the contents of memory address A2 to address A1.
SUBI A1 A2Indirect Subtraction: Subtract the contents of memory address A2 from
address A1, put the result in A2
JIF A CSet the CPU program counter with C if memory location A content is lessthan or equal to 0
PUSH APush memory A onto the stack. Stack grows downwards.
POP APop value from stack into memory A.
CALL CCall subroutine at instruction C, push return address.
RETReturn from subroutine by popping return address.
HLTHalts the CPU
USERSwitch to user mode
SYSCALL PRN ACalls the operting system service. This system call prints the contents of
memory address A to the console followed by a new line character. This
system call will block the calling thread for 100 instruction executions.
SYSCALL HLTCalls the operting system service. Shuts down the thread
SYSCALL YIELDCalls the operting system service. Yields the CPU so OS can schedule
other threads.
The numbers in the above instruction sets are signed long intergers, which means that ADD 300 -1
can be used as an instruction to decrement the memory location 300 value by 1.
The parameters for the instructions can be memory locations (A, A1, A2), unsigned long numbers
(B), or instruction numbers (C).
